words.definition: A family consisting of two parents and their children, without other relatives living with them.
words.example: In many Western countries, the nuclear family has largely replaced the extended family as the norm.
collocations: the decline of the nuclear family

words.definition: A family that includes grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins as well as parents and children.
words.example: In cultures where the extended family lives under one roof, grandparents often play a central role in raising children.

words.definition: The way in which a child is cared for and taught how to behave while growing up.
words.example: A person's upbringing has a profound influence on their values and attitudes later in life.
A certain amount of sibling rivalry is natural and may even help children develop negotiation skills.

words.definition: Describing a household in which both partners have paid jobs.
words.example: In dual-income households, finding time for regular family meals can be a genuine challenge.

words.definition: The member of a family who earns the money that the family needs to live.
words.example: The traditional model of the father as the sole breadwinner is increasingly outdated.

words.definition: The difference in attitudes, values and behaviour between older and younger people.
words.example: Rapid technological change has arguably widened the generation gap between parents and teenagers.

words.definition: The care of children by nurseries or childminders while their parents are at work.
words.example: A lack of affordable childcare forces many parents, particularly mothers, to leave the workforce.

words.definition: Time off work that a mother or father is allowed to take to look after a new baby or young child.
words.example: Offering fathers generous parental leave can encourage a more equal division of domestic responsibilities.

words.definition: Too eager to protect someone, especially a child, so that they are prevented from gaining experience.
words.example: Overprotective parents may inadvertently deny their children the chance to learn from their own mistakes.

words.definition: The ability to recover quickly from difficulties and cope with setbacks.
words.example: Allowing children to experience small failures helps them to build resilience.

words.definition: A person whose behaviour others, especially young people, admire and copy.
words.example: Parents are their children's first and most influential role models, whether they intend to be or not.

words.definition: Relating to the duties and feelings of a son or daughter towards their parents.
words.example: In many Asian cultures, caring for elderly parents is regarded as a filial duty rather than a personal choice.

words.definition: Care provided in a home where elderly or vulnerable people live and receive help from trained staff.
words.example: As families become more geographically dispersed, a growing number of elderly people are moving into residential care.

words.definition: To gradually establish a quality, feeling or idea in someone's mind.
words.example: Parents should instil a sense of responsibility in their children from an early age.

words.definition: Describing a family or home in which only one parent looks after the children.
words.example: Single-parent families are statistically more likely to experience financial hardship.

words.definition: The situation of two people living together as a couple without being married.
words.example: Rising rates of cohabitation reflect profound changes in attitudes towards marriage.
